question: Should AXorcist's `axorc` executable be supported as an independently distributed CLI, and if so should Homebrew install prebuilt release artifacts or build the Swift package from source?
rationale: The repository exposes and documents the CLI, but neither the release notes nor official tap establish a supported standalone distribution contract; choosing that contract determines the release workflow, formula design, and Peekaboo synchronization responsibilities.

options.title: Ship artifact-backed formula
options.body: Publish versioned Apple Silicon and Intel macOS CLI archives and install them through `openclaw/tap`, avoiding a Swift toolchain requirement for users.

options.title: Ship source-build formula
options.body: Add a tap formula that builds the tagged Swift package locally, accepting Xcode/Swift requirements and slower installs.

options.title: Keep manual installation
options.body: Treat `axorc` as a developer-oriented companion executable and retain the documented SwiftPM build-and-copy workflow.

recommendation.title: Ship artifact-backed formula
recommendation.body: Publish versioned Apple Silicon and Intel macOS CLI archives and install them through `openclaw/tap`, avoiding a Swift toolchain requirement for users.

likelyOwner.reason: The AXorcist release and recent CLI history most strongly points to `steipete`, and this decision affects the project's release contract.
